..summary: Orchestrator's `ares.*` subscription DLQ-loops every non-Envelope message forever

evidence: orchestrator/main.rs:139 subscribes `ares.*`, which matches ares.dlq, ares.activity and ares.vulns; main.rs:69-75 republishes every unparseable payload to SUBJECT_DLQ unconditionally — a message received ON ares.dlq that fails Envelope parsing is republished to ares.dlq and re-received, with no exit condition

Non-Envelope traffic is routine: ActivityEvent JSON from four agents and vuln advisories both fail `serde_json::from_slice::<Envelope>` (missing id/correlation_id/source/kind/payload), so every routine activity event enters an infinite DLQ republish cycle — unbounded bus amplification at the central router

delivery_count (main.rs:120-127) reads a `Nats-Delivery-Count` header nothing ever sets on core-NATS publishes, so MAX_DELIVERIES=3 can never trip; the documented 'drop only on ares.dlq after 3 deliveries' contract (docs/services.md:48) is inert
Self-republish of routed envelopes is guarded (main.rs:90 `msg.subject.as_str() == subject`) but no equivalent guard exists for ares.dlq or for non-Envelope subjects
detail.suggestion: In handle_message, return early when `msg.subject` is SUBJECT_DLQ or is not one of the routed ingress subjects (or subscribe only to `ares.alerts` plus explicit command subjects); before any DLQ republish, write an `ares-dlq-count` header and drop when it exceeds MAX_DELIVERIES — that makes the documented 3-delivery contract real and kills the loop.

..summary: vuln-agent publishes raw non-Envelope JSON on local `ares.vulns` with no consumer

evidence: main.rs:27 defines `SUBJECT_VULNS` locally and main.rs:236-249 publishes a bare json! advisory — no Envelope wrapper, breaking the platform convention that 'every service speaks the types defined' in agent-protocol (agent-protocol/lib.rs:3-4)
No subscriber to ares.vulns exists anywhere in the workspace; the payload lands on the orchestrator's ares.* subscription, fails Envelope parse, and feeds the DLQ republish loop
vuln-agent is also absent from the services.md service map and its advisory reaches consumers only through the vuln_advisories table — the NATS leg is dead boundary
detail.suggestion: Either drop the publish (the table is the real delivery channel today) or make it contractual: move SUBJECT_VULNS into agent-protocol and publish an Envelope with a suitable kind so the message participates in routing instead of the DLQ.

..summary: Four agents copy the same subscribe->spawn->envelope->span->process runtime while agent-core's runtime abstractions have zero production callers

evidence: Each agent main.rs repeats the same ~50-line runtime: tracing_subscriber init, clap Config, async_nats::connect, ConnectorConfig::from_env, nats.subscribe(SUBJECT_X), `while let Some(msg)` spawn-per-message envelope parse + info_span + process (detection-agent/main.rs:209-280, triage-agent/main.rs:362-413, hunt-agent/main.rs:181-248, response-agent/main.rs:371-429) plus the identical emit() helper

agent-core exports AgentLoop + CheckpointStore + PostgresCheckpointer + ToolGateway + Budgets, yet no production code outside the crate instantiates any of them — the intended shared boundary is bypassed in favor of per-binary machinery

api-server creates agent_checkpoints (a2a.rs:221-228 'owned by agent-core') and joins it in load_task/load_run (a2a.rs:320-346, acp.rs:159-180) to detect completed runs, but nothing writes the table — a generated-but-never-fed data path; docs/services.md:75-77 promises 'agent loop checkpoints to Postgres so restart resumes, not restarts', which is unimplemented
detail.suggestion: Extract the shared agent runtime where it belongs: add an `emit_activity`/subscribe-and-dispatch helper to agent-core (or the new activity contract module) and have the four agents adopt it; then either wire PostgresCheckpointer into a real agent loop or delete the checkpoint join in api-server and the resume-on-restart doc claim so the boundary reflects reality.

..summary: Undetected BAS results reach detection-agent twice: direct publish + orchestrator re-route of the ares.bas copy

evidence: bas-runner publishes BasResult to ares.bas unconditionally and again to ares.detection when undetected (main.rs:234-249); orchestrator route_subject maps EnvelopeKind::BasResult -> SUBJECT_DETECTION (orchestrator/main.rs:55), so the ares.bas copy is also re-published to ares.detection — two deliveries of the same envelope for every undetected scenario

detection-agent runs a full LLM-backed run_cycle for every ares.detection envelope without dedupe (main.rs:258-278), so the duplicate is real LLM spend; every detected BasResult also triggers a detection cycle via the orchestrator route even though only gaps are useful
detail.suggestion: Drop the direct ares.detection republish in bas-runner (the orchestrator already routes BasResult there) and gate the route on `payload.detected == false`, or dedupe by envelope id in detection-agent.

..summary: JetStream-first publish policy implemented twice: ingestion-gateway NatsSink vs api-server a2a.rs

evidence: api-server/a2a.rs:48,235-276 re-implements STREAM_NAME='ARES', the get-or-create `ares.>` stream config, and the JetStream-first/plain-fallback publish policy already in ingestion-gateway/nats_sink.rs:9-82 — comments openly acknowledge it ('mirrors ingestion-gateway', 'same policy as ingestion-gateway's NatsSink')
orchestrator/nats_bus.rs is a third envelope-publish wrapper (publish_envelope/publish_raw with flush); three crates now own pieces of 'how we put an Envelope on the bus'
detail.suggestion: Give the bus-publish policy one home — e.g. a `bus` module in agent-protocol or a small ares-bus crate exposing ensure_stream + publish envelope — and have NatsSink, a2a::publish and NatsBus delegate to it.

..summary: agent-core promises the agent runtime but has no role in the running system, so 'where does an agent live?' has no answer

evidence: crates/agent-core/src/lib.rs:1-7 and Cargo.toml describe the crate as 'Agent control loop, checkpointing, tool gateway and kill switch for ARES'
AgentLoop::new has zero non-test callers; HttpToolGateway, PostgresCheckpointer, Budgets, CheckpointStore, AgentError and LoopOutcome appear nowhere outside crates/agent-core (grep over crates/)

The only exports reaching production code are kill_switch_engaged (api-server/kill.rs, triage/response/vuln-agent) and the AgentState/Step types read as a DB column in api-server/src/a2a.rs:320 and api-server/src/acp.rs:159
Each of the five agents instead hand-rolls its own subscribe/spawn/LLM/tool-invoke body in main.rs (triage 413 LOC, response 429, detection 280+293, hunt 248, vuln 322)
detail.suggestion: Pick one owner for agent execution and make the crate honest about it: either wire AgentLoop/HttpToolGateway/PostgresCheckpointer into the agents (which also gives one resilience policy for /invoke), or delete agent_loop.rs, gateway.rs, budget.rs and checkpoint.rs and move AgentState/Step into agent-protocol next to Envelope, leaving agent-core as the kill-switch module or removing the crate. Do not leave a capability crate whose entire surface is unimported.

..summary: ACP landed as a second 634-line protocol front-end in api-server with no matching change to the sibling crate's shape, the rate-limit tiers, or the docs

evidence: The two protocol crates have asymmetric responsibilities: a2a owns the dispatcher and the TaskBackend seam (crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:135-157), acp owns wire types only (crates/acp/src/lib.rs:1-11), so all ACP lifecycle logic (ensure_schema, load_run, wait_terminal, SSE, cancel) sits in api-server/src/acp.rs

acp.rs reaches into a2a internals (crate::a2a::AgentDef, task_uuid, terminal_step, build_payload) rather than through a shared abstraction, so the second protocol is a sibling module of the first rather than a peer

Adding ACP required no update to crates/api-server/src/ratelimit.rs:37-45 — POST /a2a/* is Expensive but /acp/runs falls through to Tier::General, under-metering the LLM-backed run path that the rate table was written to protect (docs/services.md:97)
docs/services.md rate and contract sections gained no ACP rows (docs/services.md:94-101)
detail.suggestion: Make the two protocols peers: give acp the same shape as a2a (a transport-agnostic dispatcher + a backend trait in the acp crate, implemented by api-server) so both crates own their protocol and api-server owns only transport/persistence. Extend classify() with the ACP run/SSE routes in the same edit that adds a route, or drive tiers from the router table so the next protocol cannot skip them.

..summary: The agent roster (name, subject, envelope kind, activity name) is declared in three places and is already incomplete — vuln-agent is not in it

evidence: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:76-124 hardcodes AGENTS with subject + EnvelopeKind + activity_name + skills for exactly four agents ('The four invocable Ares agents')
crates/orchestrator/src/main.rs:49-58 separately encodes the same EnvelopeKind -> subject mapping (route_subject), so routing knowledge has two owners that can disagree silently
crates/agent-protocol/src/lib.rs:16-26 holds the subject constants but not the roster, and vuln-agent declares its own subjects locally (crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:27-29)
vuln-agent is a full pipeline agent (322 LOC, publishes advisories, opens cases) that never entered AGENTS, so it is invisible to /a2a/agents, /acp/agents and the well-known cards
detail.suggestion: Put the roster in agent-protocol next to the subject constants (name, subject, kind, activity name, description) and have both api-server's cards and orchestrator's route_subject read from it; then adding an agent is one entry, and the compiler forces the router and the interop surface to agree. Add vuln-agent as part of that move.

..summary: The ares.* subject namespace mixes Envelope and bare-JSON messages, so the orchestrator dead-letters every activity event

evidence: orchestrator/src/main.rs:139 subscribes to `ares.*` and main.rs:69-76 treats any payload that fails `serde_json::from_slice::<Envelope>` as unparseable, republishing it to `SUBJECT_DLQ` (main.rs:33).

Five agents publish `ActivityEvent` (a non-Envelope: workflow_run_id/agent/step/detail/ts) on `ares.activity` — detection-agent/src/activity.rs:8, hunt-agent, response-agent, triage-agent, vuln-agent/src/main.rs:29 — and vuln-agent publishes a bare advisory object on `ares.vulns` (vuln-agent/src/main.rs:236-250).
Every other producer on `ares.*` publishes an `Envelope`: ingestion-gateway/src/main.rs:100, bas-runner/src/main.rs:236-245, triage-agent/src/main.rs:225-233, api-server/src/a2a.rs:269-272.
Consequence: `ares.*` is a single-level wildcard, so each activity and vulns message is parsed, rejected, and re-published to `ares.dlq`, which nothing consumes.
detail.suggestion: Stop matching the non-Envelope subjects: subscribe the orchestrator to the explicit routed subjects (`ares.alerts|triage|respond|detection|hunt|bas`) instead of `ares.*`, and document in agent-protocol/src/lib.rs that `ares.activity` and `ares.vulns` are out-of-band feeds.

..summary: Cargo manifests split 7/14 between brace-style workspace deps with metadata and dotted-style without

evidence: a2a, acp, agent-core, agent-protocol, audit, cvss, llm-client declare `serde = { workspace = true }` plus a `description` and `rust-version.workspace = true` (e.g. crates/a2a/Cargo.toml:6-14).
The other 14 declare `serde.workspace = true` with no `description` and no `rust-version` (e.g. crates/connectors/Cargo.toml:9-16, crates/api-server/Cargo.toml:6-26).
The split is not lib-vs-bin: connectors, enrichment-lib, http-limits and policy-engine are libraries that follow the bin style, so 4 of 11 libraries contradict the other 7.

`#![warn(missing_docs)]` tracks the same 7-crate group (present in agent-protocol:8, agent-core:9, a2a:8, acp:9, audit:12, llm-client:8; absent from cvss, connectors, enrichment-lib, http-limits, policy-engine), so the doc-completeness lint covers only part of the library surface.

agent-core/Cargo.toml:17-19 and audit/Cargo.toml:15-17 both re-declare sqlx inline with a comment explaining that the workspace spec requests a nonexistent `pgvector` feature — a documented workaround that leaves two crates outside the centralised-dependency convention.
detail.suggestion: Pick one manifest style (dotted is the majority at 14/21) and apply it to all 21 crates, add `description` to the 14 that lack one, and add `#![warn(missing_docs)]` to the five libraries that already document everything by hand.

..summary: Three agents re-implement the LLM completion + fence-strip + parse sequence with different fence handling

evidence: detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:32-56, triage-agent/src/main.rs:105-127 and response-agent/src/main.rs:136-157 each build a `CompletionRequest`, call `router.complete`, then hand-roll `.trim().trim_start_matches("```json")...trim_end_matches("```")` before parsing.

The three copies have already diverged: pipeline.rs:48-50 also strips ```yaml and ```yml (needed for Sigma drafting) while the two JSON consumers strip only ```json and ``` — so an uppercase ```JSON fence or a ` ``` json` variant is handled by none of them.

llm-client (the crate that owns provider interaction) exposes no helper for this, so each agent re-derives the protocol; detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:35 and response-agent/src/main.rs:139 are also flagged as a boilerplate-duplication pair.
detail.suggestion: Add one `llm_client::complete_json<T: DeserializeOwned>(router, tier, req) -> Result<T>` (or a `strip_fences` + `complete_text` pair, ~15 lines) that strips an optional case-insensitive fence with an optional language tag, and call it from the three sites.

..summary: Task/run/advisory state transitions discard DB errors with `let _ = sqlx::query(...)` in six places

evidence: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:336-341 marks a task 'completed' during load_task with the result ignored; if the UPDATE fails the task reports 'working' forever.

crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:441-447 and crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:266-279 mark a task/run 'failed' after a publish error, also ignoring the write error — the failure path can itself fail silently.

crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:616-621 (SSE terminal write-back), crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:170-177 (checkpoint fold-in), crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:272-278 (case_id write-back) follow the same pattern.

Every neighbouring read in the same functions propagates instead (`map_err(|e| BackendError::Internal(e.to_string()))` at crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:311, 322), so within one function errors are sometimes fatal and sometimes invisible.
detail.suggestion: Route these six writes through one small helper that logs at `warn!`/`error!` on failure (the idempotency store already does this: crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:118-120), and propagate where the caller can still return an error.

..summary: Documented `{error: string}` envelope is honored only by the rate limiter; siblings return plain text, bare status, or `{code, message}`

evidence: docs/services.md:37-38 states the contract: "Errors: JSON `{error: string}`; 4xx = caller fixable, 5xx = retryable."
15 handlers in crates/api-server/src/main.rs, vulns.rs, playbooks.rs and coverage.rs return `(StatusCode, String)` (e.g. main.rs:125, vulns.rs:73), which axum serializes as text/plain — not JSON.

crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:50-56 and its nine `(StatusCode, Json<AcpError>)` sites return `{code, message}`; crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:508-513 returns a bare `StatusCode::NOT_FOUND` with an empty body while a2a.rs:548 returns `(StatusCode, String)`.
crates/ingestion-gateway/src/main.rs:110-121 returns `{id, status, error}` and uses 502 where docs/services.md:36 specifies 503 when NATS is down.

Internal failures are reported as gateway errors: `list_audit` (crates/api-server/src/main.rs:197) and `get_plan` (main.rs:268) map Postgres errors to BAD_GATEWAY, so a 5xx no longer tells the caller whether to retry a dependency or report a server bug.
detail.suggestion: Add one `ApiError` type in api-server implementing `IntoResponse` (status + `{error}` body, internals logged not echoed) and convert the 15 `(StatusCode, String)` handlers plus the ACP/a2a error returns to it; that is fewer shapes than exist today, not more.

..summary: Unparseable messages go to the DLQ but unroutable ones are only logged, and DLQ publish errors are ignored

evidence: crates/orchestrator/src/main.rs:70-78 sends a parse failure to `ares.dlq`, but crates/orchestrator/src/main.rs:105-109 logs `failed to route envelope` and drops the message with no DLQ copy.
Both DLQ publishes are `let _ = bus.publish_raw(SUBJECT_DLQ, ...)` (lines 65 and 73), so a DLQ publish failure loses the alert with no record beyond the preceding warn.

The two drop paths therefore have different durability guarantees for the same outcome (message not delivered downstream), which is exactly the case the docs' 'drop only on `ares.dlq` after 3 deliveries' note (docs/services.md:46) promises.
detail.suggestion: Route the publish failure at line 105 through the same `publish_raw(SUBJECT_DLQ, ...)` path as the parse failure, and `error!` (not `let _ =`) when the DLQ publish itself fails.

..summary: BAS measurement treats query/DB errors as 'not detected' and persists that as the scenario result

evidence: crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:130-145 `wait_mttd` warns on an OpenSearch error and keeps polling, then returns `None` at timeout — indistinguishable from 'the detection never fired'.
crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:150-167 `wait_mttr` uses `fetch_one(pool).await.unwrap_or(0)`, so a Postgres error is read as 'no containment seen'.

crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:184-200 derives `detected = mttd.is_some()` and writes the row into `bas_results`, so an outage during a run is recorded permanently as a detection failure and skews the MTTD/MTTR metrics served by crates/api-server/src/main.rs:215-250.
detail.suggestion: Return `Result<Option<u64>>`/`Result<(Option<i64>, bool)>` from `wait_mttd`/`wait_mttr`, propagate with `?` so `run_scenario` fails and the row is not written (the caller already logs per-scenario failures at crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:294-299).

..summary: `process` names the whole per-envelope handler in two agents while three sibling binaries use distinct, descriptive verbs

evidence: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:253 `async fn process(deps: &Deps, envelope: &Envelope)` runs IOC extraction, enrichment, the LLM verdict, case creation and handoff
crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:235 `async fn process(deps: &Deps, envelope: &Envelope)` builds a plan and executes every action
Siblings name the same concept concretely: `run_cycle` (crates/detection-agent/src/main.rs:138), `run_sweep` (crates/hunt-agent/src/main.rs:131), `handle_message` (crates/orchestrator/src/main.rs:61)
The triage call site reads `process(&deps, &envelope).instrument(span).await` (main.rs:404), giving no hint of what is processed or into what
detail.suggestion: Rename both to `handle_envelope` (or `triage_envelope` / `respond_to_envelope`) and use one verb for the per-envelope entry point across the five binaries, so a reader moving between agent crates finds the same name for the same role.

..summary: `Impact::{Read, Write, High}` mixes an access kind with an intensity, so `Impact::High` reads wrong at every guard

evidence: crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:69-73 `pub enum Impact { Read, Write, High }` — two variants classify access, the third classifies severity
crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:375 `if tool.policy.impact != Impact::Read` reads as "not read" but means "write or high impact"
The YAML vocabulary in policies/tools.yml uses `high` alongside `read`/`write`, so the wire value is fixed even if the Rust variant is clarified
detail.suggestion: Rename the variant to `HighImpact` (keeping `#[serde(rename = "high")]` so policies/tools.yml is unchanged) so the enum reads as one axis: Read, Write, HighImpact.

..summary: Two insert-and-report helpers return bools with opposite meanings (true = duplicate vs true = newly inserted)

evidence: crates/orchestrator/src/dedupe.rs:33-41 `check_and_mark` inserts the key and returns `Ok(res.rows_affected() == 0)`, i.e. true means already seen
crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:161-185 `record_advisory` inserts the advisory and returns `Ok(inserted.is_some())`, i.e. true means new
The orchestrator call site needs the doc comment to disambiguate: `Ok(true) => { info!("duplicate alert; skipped") }` (orchestrator/src/main.rs:94-98)
detail.suggestion: Put the polarity in the name: `mark_seen_and_report_duplicate` in dedupe.rs (still true = duplicate) and `insert_advisory_if_new` in vuln-agent, so both call sites read correctly without consulting the docstring.

..summary: Executor structs drift from the tool names they serve, and only 2 of ~20 carry a `Tool` suffix

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:564 `struct NvdTool` and :633 `struct CvssScoreTool` are the only two executor types with a `Tool` suffix; the rest are MispSearch (:183), ThehiveCase (:103), WazuhAgents (:314), SlackNotify (:532)

crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:649 `struct DryRun` is the stub executor for tools with no backend; its name describes the JSON payload it returns (`dry_run(args)` at :35) rather than the executor
crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:103 `ThehiveCase` serves the tool name `thehive.case.create` (returned at :108), so the type name and the tool name diverge
The registry at :668-779 pairs each type with a different tool name in some cases (MispAttribute serves both `misp.attribute.add` and `misp.ioc.block`)
detail.suggestion: Drop the suffix (`NvdLookup`, `CvssScore`) so all executors follow the verb/noun pattern of their neighbours, rename `DryRun` to `StubExecutor`, and make each struct name a readable contraction of the tool it registers (`ThehiveCaseCreate`).

..summary: Tool argument names drift per executor and are masked by alias lists of two to six keys

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:194 and :241 the MISP search tools accept `["value", "ioc", "query"]` for the same argument
crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:398 ProviderLookup accepts `["ioc", "value", "ip", "domain", "hash", "url"]` — six names for one input
crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:177 CortexAnalyzer accepts `["data", "observable"]` and :131 accepts `["case_id", "id"]`, so no single canonical name exists per concept
detail.suggestion: Declare one canonical argument name per concept in each executor's doc comment (`ioc`, `case_id`, `data`) and trim the alias lists to canonical + at most one legacy spelling, so a developer or planner prompt has a single name to target.

..summary: ModelRouter's two-provider tiering is constructed with one provider and called with one fixed tier at every site

evidence: All three construction sites pass the same provider twice: ModelRouter::new(provider.clone(), provider) (response-agent/src/main.rs:398, detection-agent/src/main.rs:225, triage-agent/src/main.rs:379)
Each call site hardcodes one tier: router.complete(ModelTier::Strong, ..) in detection/pipeline.rs:43 and response-agent/main.rs:147; router.complete(ModelTier::Fast, ..) in triage-agent/main.rs:116
route() (llm-client/src/lib.rs:137) is only reachable through complete(), so the fast/strong fields and the ModelTier parameter never select anything different
detail.suggestion: Replace `router: Arc<ModelRouter>` with `Arc<dyn LlmProvider>` in the three agents and call provider.complete(&req) directly; keep fast_model()/strong_model() as the tier signal since they already pick the model name. Re-introduce a router only when a genuinely different provider backs a tier.

..summary: Three NATS publish wrappers plus a fourth inline helper, with JetStream bootstrap duplicated

evidence: NatsSink::connect/ensure_stream/publish (ingestion-gateway/src/nats_sink.rs:27-75) and a2a::ensure_jetstream/publish (api-server/src/a2a.rs:207-270) implement the same 'JetStream if the ARES stream exists, else plain publish' policy with STREAM_NAME="ARES" declared in both files
NatsBus (orchestrator/src/nats_bus.rs) is a three-method forwarder: subscribe and publish_envelope delegate to the client, publish_raw adds only flush()
bas-runner has its own publish helper that always uses plain NATS (crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:171-183), so envelope transport differs per service
detail.suggestion: Keep one JetStream-first publisher (move NatsSink into agent-protocol or a small nats-support crate) and have api-server, orchestrator and bas-runner use it; delete NatsBus and the bas-runner helper.

..summary: EvalCtx.asset_classes is a public field no production code fills, making the protected host-class check unreachable

evidence: EvalCtx.asset_classes is a pub HashMap<String,String> (policy-engine/src/lib.rs:46); its only writer in the repo is the unit test at lib.rs:630

tool-server constructs EvalCtx::new() once and never inserts into asset_classes (tool-server/src/main.rs:99-102), so the branch at lib.rs:450 (`host_classes.contains(class)`) can never match, even though policies/protected-assets.yml declares host_classes: [domain_controller, pki_ca, siem_node, soar_control]
The whole context sits behind AppState's Mutex<EvalCtx> (tool-server/src/main.rs:37), serializing every policy evaluation so that a single-threaded map can be mutated by callers that do not exist
detail.suggestion: Drop asset_classes from EvalCtx and resolve host classes inside PolicyEngine::load from protected-assets.yml (or a loaded asset inventory), so the check works without a context field. Then EvalCtx holds only the Arc<DashMap> counters and the outer Mutex can go.

..summary: Byte-identical utility helpers (b64url, ratelimit::build, hex encoding) are duplicated across crates instead of shared

evidence: `fn b64url` is 21 lines and byte-identical in crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:54-74 and crates/enrichment-lib/src/lib.rs:172-192 (verified with diff); both encode VirusTotal URL ids.

`pub fn build() -> Arc<RateLimiter>` is byte-identical in crates/api-server/src/ratelimit.rs:11-17 and crates/ingestion-gateway/src/ratelimit.rs:11-17, including the POLICIES_DIR resolution and the spawn_idle_purge call.

Lowercase-hex encoding is written five times: crates/audit/src/lib.rs:141-145 (`sha256_hex`), crates/orchestrator/src/dedupe.rs:83-86 (a whole `mod hex` justified as 'to avoid an extra dependency'), crates/tool-server/src/idempotency.rs:117-121, crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:367-369 (`fn hex`), and inline in enrichment-lib's Sha256 formatting.
Each copy is small enough that no single one looks wrong, so the cost only appears when one needs a fix (padding, uppercase, error handling) and four call sites silently keep the old behaviour.
detail.suggestion: Move `b64url` and a hex encoder into one leaf crate both callers already depend on (connectors for b64url, agent-protocol for hex), and turn the duplicated `ratelimit::build` into `http_limits::build(classify: fn(&Request) -> Tier)` so api-server and ingestion-gateway pass only their classifier.

..summary: The severity → TheHive integer mapping is written twice with different defaults (2 vs 0) for the same unknown input

evidence: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:173-178 maps low=1, high=3, critical=4 and everything else (including medium and any unrecognized string) to 2.

crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:86-94 defines `severity_rank` mapping low=1..critical=4 with `_ => 0`, and line 258 reuses that comparison rank as the case's `severity` field (`severity: severity_rank(&severity)`), so an unrecognized severity produces a TheHive case with severity 0 instead of the triage agent's 2.

The two functions also disagree on ordering semantics: triage's version is a presentation mapping that skips 2 for 'medium' by falling into `_`, vuln's is a comparison rank — one function is doing two jobs.
detail.suggestion: Put a single `fn case_severity(sev: &str) -> u8` next to `NewCase` in the connectors crate (low=1, medium=2, high=3, critical=4, unknown=2) and have both agents call it; keep vuln-agent's `severity_rank` only for the `>= min_rank` comparison.

..summary: enrich_cve hand-rolls the Redis get/set logic in four nested if-lets while cache_get/cache_set sit unused ten lines above

..summary: Triage passes the case id to response only inside a thehive:// URI; the receiver defaults the id to "unknown"

..summary: The orchestrator subscribes to ares.* which includes its own DLQ subject, so unparseable messages republish forever

evidence: crates/orchestrator/src/main.rs:133 subscribes to "ares.*", and SUBJECT_DLQ is "ares.dlq" (main.rs:35), which the wildcard matches.

On a parse failure main.rs:79-83 publishes the raw payload to SUBJECT_DLQ; the orchestrator receives its own publish, delivery_count() returns 1 when no Nats-Delivery-Count header is present (main.rs:120-128), the payload still fails to parse, and it is published again - an unbounded loop with no delay.

ares.activity messages are ActivityEvent JSON, never Envelope JSON, so every activity event in the pipeline takes that path (producers: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:79-91 and the other four agents).

..summary: EvalCtx.asset_classes is never populated, so the protected host-class rule is dead; the &mut signature also forces a global mutex

..summary: Connector clients expose only some verbs, so three callers hand-roll HTTP with their own credential reads

evidence: OpensearchClient exposes only query (crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:147-157), so crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:146-157 and crates/detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:234-241 each POST raw with their own OPENSEARCH_URL/USER/PASS reads.

..summary: The policy->audit->idempotency->execute composition in tool-server /invoke has no test

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:60 `invoke` is the only path to side effects in the system; the file contains no #[cfg(test)] module.

evidence: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:253 `process` routes an LLM verdict to `write_fp_verdict`, `open_case` or `handoff_respond` and is gated by the kill switch; the crate reports 0 tests (`running 0 tests` in cargo test).

..summary: connectors (1,189 LOC, 6 HTTP clients) tests only JSON parsing; retry, budget and throttle logic is unverified

evidence: The 3 tests at crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:1141-1188 cover MISP attribute deserialization and warning-list matching only.

`retry_sleep` (line 67) and the `call` retry loop with `CALL_BUDGET` (lines 84-120) implement backoff and deadline handling; a regression here means either hammering a SOAR API or timing out silently, and nothing asserts the schedule or the give-up path.

..summary: detection-agent pipeline has zero tests for Sigma validation, Lucene conversion and rule promotion

evidence: crates/detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs has no #[cfg(test)] module despite containing pure functions: `validate_sigma` (line 60) enforces required keys, `to_lucene` (111) and `naive_lucene` (131) convert Sigma to a query, `slugify` (283) builds file names.

..summary: orchestrator dedupe key/day-bucket logic is untested; a wrong key silently drops or duplicates alerts

evidence: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs (640 LOC) and crates/api-server/src/acp.rs (634 LOC) contain no tests; the single api-server test (main.rs:387) only calls `api_router()` to prove route path syntax compiles.

evidence: evals/policy_tests.md rows 8 (protected CIDR via `firewall.rule.add`), 9 (enum violation), 15 (control-plane `self.services`), 16 (missing required arg on `kill_process`), 17 (`rule_path` pattern), 18 (CVE-id pattern) and 19 (CVSS vector pattern) have no corresponding test in crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:536-723.

evidence: `PolicyEngine::kill_switch_engaged` (crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:426) returns true when `ARES_KILL_SWITCH` is truthy, and `evaluate_inner` checks it first (line 329).

..summary: api-server returns three different error-body shapes (plain text, typed ACP error, empty) despite one documented contract

evidence: docs/services.md:37 states the contract: 'Errors: JSON `{error: string}`; 4xx = caller fixable, 5xx = retryable.'
Console/vuln/playbook handlers return `(StatusCode, String)` -> `text/plain` bodies (crates/api-server/src/main.rs:111-137, vulns.rs:49-121, playbooks.rs:70-82).

..summary: Tool arguments are specified twice — JSON Schema in policies/tools.yml and alias lists in executors — and no schema is exposed by the API

evidence: 17 tools carry `args_schema` with `additionalProperties: false` (policies/tools.yml:32-38,42-47,81-116,122-167), so only the canonical key names can ever reach an executor.

Executors nonetheless accept undocumented aliases: `arg_str(args, &["value", "ioc", "query"])` (executors/mod.rs:190), `&["case_id", "id"]` (:126), `&["q", "query_string"]` (:97), `&["cve_id", "id", "cve"]` (:583), plus shape polymorphism ('`{case_id, observable}` or flat fields', :131-136) and `values` vs `value` fallbacks (:280-296).

`GET /tools` returns names only (`Json<Vec<String>>`, crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:208), and `PolicyEngine` keeps validators private, exposing only `tool_names()` (crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:305).

..summary: AuditWriter::append takes six positional parameters, four of them adjacent &str, and takes the decision as a string

evidence: `pub async fn append(&self, actor: &str, tool: &str, args: &Value, decision: &str, reason: &str, correlation_id: Uuid)` (crates/audit/src/lib.rs:59-67) — six parameters, with `actor`/`tool`/`decision`/`reason` all plain `&str`.

Callers must pre-convert the domain enum: `decision_label(&decision.kind)` at crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:90-98, and the reject path hardcodes the literal `"deny"` (crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:349).

..summary: POST /controls/kill-switch silently engages on a malformed body and returns different fields than the GET

evidence: `serde_json::from_slice::<KillBody>(&body).map(|b| b.engaged).unwrap_or(true)` (crates/api-server/src/kill.rs:41-46) — any malformed or misspelled payload engages the kill switch instead of returning 400.

..summary: All three HTTP services accept anonymous requests; the only gate is per-tool policy

evidence: crates/api-server/src/main.rs:283-325 lists 27 routes including POST /controls/kill-switch, POST /a2a/{agent}, POST /acp/runs and GET /audit; main.rs:361-367 applies only http_limits::middleware and CorsLayer::permissive().
crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:274-281 serves /invoke, /tools and /approvals/{id}/approve|reject with no authentication; infra/docker-compose.yml:330 publishes 8090:8090 to the host.

..summary: A2A agent cards advertise bearer auth that the server never enforces

evidence: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:158-160 sets Authentication { schemes: vec!["bearer"] } for every agent card built by card_for().
crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:189-191 sets the same scheme on the platform card returned by /.well-known/agent.json.

..summary: Global kill switch: no auth, no audit row, and the file it writes is not the one policy reads

evidence: crates/api-server/src/kill.rs:39-72 writes or removes $POLICIES_DIR/kill from an unauthenticated POST, taking the body as raw Bytes and defaulting an empty body to engaged=true.
No actor is captured and no audit_log row is written, while every tool decision is appended to the hash chain (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:82-99).

infra/docker-compose.yml:311-330 mounts ../policies:/policies:ro into tool-server, but api-server (:341-348) has no policies mount, so its write lands in its own container filesystem and policy-engine's read at crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:452 never sees it.
crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:443-456 also honours ARES_KILL_SWITCH, giving two independent switch states with no reconciliation.
detail.suggestion: Gate the POST behind the shared auth layer, append an audit_log event with the caller identity on every engage/disengage, and propagate state through one channel the enforcer reads (a NATS control subject or a writable shared volume), not a per-container file.

..summary: Approver identity comes from the request body and defaults to 'operator'; no separation of duties

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:213-216 reads `approver` from the optional JSON body and falls back to "operator".
crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:276-279 does the same for reject.
The resulting string is written as the audit actor (approvals.rs:248-255 for approve, 299-308 for reject), so the human-approval record proves only that someone reached an unauthenticated port.
Nothing compares the approver with the parked call's own `actor`, so the caller that submitted a call can approve it.
detail.suggestion: Derive the approver from the authenticated principal (the same middleware that fixes the authn gap) instead of the body, reject approve/reject when no principal is present, and refuse an approval whose principal equals call.actor to enforce separation of duties.

..summary: ToolCall.actor is caller-supplied and ignored by the policy engine, so authz is per-tool only

..summary: idem_key round-trips a String through serde_json::to_value to re-extract the same string

..summary: Infallible serialization is guarded with unwrap_or_default, turning bugs into empty 200 bodies and empty SSE data

evidence: Every workspace member is a library, yet two are named with suffixes: crates/enrichment-lib (actually IoC extraction + 5-provider enrichment fan-out + Redis caching) and crates/http-limits (per-key token buckets + SSE concurrency caps + tier config).

Sibling crates are named after the domain they own (connectors, cvss, audit, policy-engine, agent-protocol), so the suffix pattern gives no signal about contents and does not match the documented ownership model in docs/services.md.
enrichment-lib is also a single 579-line module holding three responsibilities (extract_iocs, Enricher::enrich fan-out, cache_key), so the vague name hides a flat file as well.
detail.suggestion: Rename crates/enrichment-lib to crates/enrichment (or crates/ioc-enrichment) and split its lib.rs into iocs.rs, providers.rs and cache.rs; leave http-limits as-is if the name is meant to mark it as a mechanism crate, otherwise rename to http-ratelimit. Renames touch Cargo.toml members, the 4 dependent Cargo.toml path deps and `use enrichment_lib` call sites; validate with `cargo metadata --no-deps` and `cargo test --workspace`.

..summary: PolicyEngine reads ARES_KILL_SWITCH from ambient env per evaluation, making its test suite environment-dependent

evidence: crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:346 calls `self.kill_switch_engaged()` inside `evaluate_inner`, which reads `std::env::var("ARES_KILL_SWITCH")` at :444 on every call.

Tests asserting Allow/ApprovalRequired - `blast_radius_cap_is_enforced` (:671), `cooldown_blocks_repeat_same_target` (:696), `allowlisted_tool_is_allowed` (:716), `misp_writes_require_approval` (:731) - fail if the developer or CI environment exports `ARES_KILL_SWITCH=1`.
No injection seam exists: `PolicyEngine::load(dir)` takes only a path, and the tool server passes nothing else (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:225-226).
detail.suggestion: Capture the switch state in the engine at construction (e.g. `PolicyEngine::load(dir)` records the env flag, or add `with_kill_switch(bool)`) and let the per-evaluation file check stay; tests then construct the engine with `kill_switch: false` and stop depending on process env.

..summary: Boot-time ConnectorConfig and per-call env::var resolve the same keys with different semantics

evidence: crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:42-44 filters empty env values, so `ConnectorConfig` maps an empty `THEHIVE_API_KEY` to `Auth::None`; crates/api-server/src/main.rs:142-143 uses `env::var("THEHIVE_API_KEY").unwrap_or_default()` and always calls `.bearer_auth(key)`, sending an empty bearer token.

crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:233-238 re-reads `OPENSEARCH_USER`/`OPENSEARCH_PASS` per verdict write while `deps.os` was built from `ConnectorConfig` at boot (main.rs:461-470), so the raw write path and the client path can authenticate differently.
crates/detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:208-216 re-reads `OPENSEARCH_URL`/`USER`/`PASS` per monitor deploy, duplicating the boot-resolved `deps.os` config.

crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:378 and :388 decide dry-run vs real execution from `env(..)` inside `execute`, so credentials are resolved at request time while connector clients were resolved at boot in `build_registry` (:674).
detail.suggestion: Resolve every credential once at boot and carry it: store `conn_cfg` in `AppState`/`Deps` and pass the resolved base URL and `Auth` into `thehive_query`, `write_fp_verdict`, `deploy_monitor`, and the executor structs (as `Option<String>` fields set in `build_registry`) instead of calling `env::var` inside handlers and `execute`.

..summary: Repo-relative data paths are resolved against process CWD with no boot validation, and one path is duplicated across crates

evidence: `ACTIVE_DIR = "detection-content/active"` is declared twice - crates/api-server/src/coverage.rs:12 and crates/detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:17 - with no shared owner, so writer and reader are coupled only by a string literal.

`SCENARIOS_DIR = "bas/scenarios"` (crates/bas-runner/src/scenario.rs:8) and the `policies`/`playbooks` defaults (crates/api-server/src/playbooks.rs:12-14, crates/api-server/src/kill.rs:28) are CWD-relative with no canonicalization.

Failure is silent: crates/api-server/src/coverage.rs:23-29 returns an empty technique list with a note, and crates/bas-runner/src/scenario.rs:40-44 returns an empty scenario list, so a service started from the wrong directory looks healthy.
detail.suggestion: Add one `data_dir`-style field to each service's clap `Config` (env-backed, defaulting to the repo root paths), resolve it once at boot with `canonicalize()`, and fail fast when it is missing; define the active-content path once and have api-server take it from config instead of a second const.

..summary: Enricher::new() reads env and builds ConnectorConfig internally with no injection point

evidence: crates/enrichment-lib/src/lib.rs:213-230 reads `REDIS_URL`, `VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY`, `ABUSEIPDB_API_KEY`, `SHODAN_API_KEY`, `GREYNOISE_API_KEY` and calls `ConnectorConfig::from_env()` inside `new()`, so construction silently depends on ambient process state.

There is no constructor taking explicit config, and no test constructs an `Enricher` (crates/enrichment-lib/src/lib.rs:525-579 covers only pure helpers), so the env-dependent construction is untestable.
`redis::Client::open(u).ok()` at :218 silently drops a malformed `REDIS_URL`, leaving caching disabled with no log.
The codebase's own convention is the opposite: `AnthropicProvider::new(api_key)` plus a separate `from_env()` (crates/llm-client/src/anthropic.rs:23-42).
detail.suggestion: Split into `Enricher::new(cfg: EnricherConfig)` (explicit keys and redis URL) plus `Enricher::from_env()`, and call `from_env()` only from the service `main` functions that build `Deps`/`AppState`; log instead of dropping an unparsable `REDIS_URL`.

..summary: Process-global EvalCtx is created empty at boot and its asset_classes are never loaded, disabling the protected-host-class rule

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:52 holds `eval_ctx: Mutex<EvalCtx>` and :271 constructs it with `EvalCtx::new()`, which starts with an empty `asset_classes` map (crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:52-56).

Nothing populates `asset_classes` in production code - the only writer is a test at crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:647 - so the check at :467 can never match and a protected host class never denies a call.
The same singleton is mutated under a mutex per invoke (crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:78-80), coupling all requests through one global context.
detail.suggestion: Load host->asset-class mappings at boot (from `protected-assets.yml` or the Wazuh inventory) into `AppState` alongside the engine and seed `EvalCtx` from it; if no source exists, delete the field and the unreachable branch instead of shipping a global that can never be satisfied.

..summary: Four agent crates copy-paste the same activity event, emit helper and envelope subscribe loop; a fifth emits an incompatible shape

evidence: crates/{detection,hunt,response}-agent/src/activity.rs are byte-identical 44-line modules (same SUBJECT_ACTIVITY, same ActivityEvent); triage-agent/src/activity.rs:27 differs only by `step: &'static str`, so the copies have already drifted.

crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:29 declares a fifth SUBJECT_ACTIVITY constant and crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:120-133 emits an ad-hoc json! without workflow_run_id, which the run filters at api-server/src/a2a.rs:610 and acp.rs:559 can never match.
`async fn emit` is duplicated verbatim at detection-agent/main.rs:72, hunt-agent/main.rs:55, response-agent/main.rs:86 and triage-agent/main.rs:79.

The subscribe -> tokio::spawn -> parse Envelope -> info_span!(workflow_run_id, envelope_id) block is duplicated at detection-agent/main.rs:258-278, hunt-agent/main.rs:213-239, response-agent/main.rs:409-427 and triage-agent/main.rs:483-504.
detail.suggestion: Move ActivityEvent, SUBJECT_ACTIVITY and emit into agent-protocol (already the shared protocol crate) and make all five agents — including vuln-agent — use it; then add one `spawn_envelope_consumer(nats, subject, span_name, handler)` in agent-core so each main's consume loop is ~10 lines.

..summary: A2A and ACP modules duplicate the same task/run persistence fold and SSE relay state machine

evidence: a2a.rs:583-630 task_events and acp.rs:536-577 run_stream are the same `futures::stream::unfold` machine: identical St fields (rx, pool, run_id/corr, agent, replay, closing, done), same workflow_run_id filter, same terminal_step check, same Lagged->continue, same 15s KeepAlive.
a2a.rs:306-364 load_task and acp.rs:144-183 load_run are the same row-load + agent_checkpoints fold + completed write-back, differing only in table name and struct.

a2a.rs:482-494 and acp.rs:447-484 repeat the same `UPDATE ... WHERE state NOT IN ('completed','failed','canceled')` and carry the same duplicated 'known gap: agents never poll a cancellation table' comment.
The two files are the crate's largest (631 and 634 LOC) and each re-implements the terminal-step -> completed write-back.
detail.suggestion: Extract one module in api-server (e.g. `run_relay`) holding (a) a `RelayState` enum replacing the replay/closing/done booleans, (b) a generic `sse_relay(corr_id, agent, replay, event_fn, reload_fn)` and (c) one terminal write-back helper; parameterize over (table, row type, event shape) for the two protocols.

..summary: Three agents repeat the same CompletionRequest construction and markdown-fence stripping; llm-client offers no helper

evidence: triage-agent/src/main.rs:106-124, response-agent/src/main.rs:138-155 and detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:33-52 each build CompletionRequest { system, one user message of serde_json::to_string(context), max_tokens, temperature: 0.0 }, call router.complete(tier), then run the trim/trim_start_matches("```json")/trim_end_matches("```") chain and parse.
agent-core/src/agent_loop.rs:121-130 is a fourth copy of the request construction.
The fence-strip chain differs only in which language tags each site lists, so any fix (e.g. an unterminated fence) has to be applied three times.
detail.suggestion: Add `ModelRouter::complete_json(tier, system: &str, context: &Value, max_tokens: u32) -> Result<String, LlmError>` to crates/llm-client/src/lib.rs that builds the request and strips code fences once; the three call sites collapse to a single line each.

..summary: coverage.rs and playbooks.rs duplicate the same directory-scan-and-parse YAML block

evidence: coverage.rs:25-58 and playbooks.rs:26-58 repeat the identical read_dir -> yml/yaml extension filter -> read_to_string -> serde_yaml::from_str::<Value> -> collect-errors loop (the 11-line window the detector flagged).
The unreadable-directory case is handled two different ways: a `note` field in coverage's JSON body versus an `errors` entry in playbooks.
detail.suggestion: Add one helper in api-server, e.g. `fn yaml_docs(dir: &str) -> (Vec<(PathBuf, Value)>, Vec<String>)`, and have both handlers map its result; leave crates/bas-runner/src/scenario.rs alone because it deserializes into a typed Scenario.

..summary: v31::score and v40::score duplicate the same metric-map validation loop

evidence: cvss/src/v31.rs:135-152 and cvss/src/v40.rs:213-228 both split the vector, look each key up in their VALID table (InvalidToken), check the value list (InvalidValue) and insert into a HashMap (Duplicate on overwrite).
The two copies differ only in the local variable name (map vs sel) and the table constant.
detail.suggestion: Move the loop into crates/cvss/src/lib.rs as `fn metric_map(pairs: MetricPairs, valid: &[(&str, &[&str])]) -> Result<HashMap<String, String>, CvssError>` and call it from both scorers.

..summary: Status::Approved is documented as 'approved and the call was executed' but is set before the post-approval policy re-check

evidence: Status::Approved doc: 'A human approved and the call was executed' (crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:39-40)
approve() settles the record to Approved first (218-227) and only then re-evaluates policy (230-233); when the re-check returns Deny the result is a failure stub and nothing executes (235-243)
The record keeps status Approved with an error result, so `GET /approvals?status=approved` lists calls that were never performed
detail.suggestion: Either add a distinct terminal status for 'approved but blocked by re-check' (or set Rejected/Failed when the re-check denies), or soften the doc to 'a human approved and execution was attempted'.

..summary: severity_from_level documents clamping out-of-range levels but silently downgrades them to 'medium'

evidence: Doc: 'Maps a decision-model severity level (0–3, probability-weighted) to the verdict severity label, clamping out-of-range values' (crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:147-149)
Implementation clamps only the low end (`level.round().max(0.0)`) and falls back to "medium" when the index is out of range (149-155), so a level of 4.0 yields 'medium' instead of the top band
The downgrade is behavioral: severity_gte_high() then suppresses the handoff to response-agent for an alert the model scored at maximum severity (66-68, 439-447)
detail.suggestion: Clamp both ends — `SEVERITY_LEVELS.get(level.round().clamp(0.0, 3.0) as usize)` — so an out-of-range high level resolves to 'critical', matching the docstring.

..summary: RunMode::Sync promises to block until a terminal state, but api-server returns after 120s with a non-terminal run and HTTP 200

evidence: RunMode::Sync doc: 'Block until the run reaches a terminal state' (crates/acp/src/lib.rs:186-190)

api-server wraps the wait in `tokio::time::timeout(SYNC_TIMEOUT, ...)` and ignores the elapsed result, then returns whatever state the row is in with StatusCode::OK (crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:47-48, 185-218, 390-395)
A client following the type contract cannot distinguish 'finished' from 'still running' without re-reading `status`
detail.suggestion: Document the timeout in the RunMode::Sync contract (e.g. 'blocks until terminal or SYNC_TIMEOUT, returning the live run') or return 202 instead of 200 when the timeout elapses so the wire response matches the promised semantics.

..summary: --dry skips execution but still records detected=false rows and publishes coverage-gap envelopes that trigger detection-agent

evidence: crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:93-99: `execute` logs and returns Ok(()) when the transport env var is unset or `dry` is true.

crates/bas-runner/src/main.rs:186-243: run_scenario proceeds regardless of `deps.dry`, waits up to 600s for MTTD, inserts one `bas_results` row per technique with `detected=false`, and republishes the payload to SUBJECT_DETECTION when `!detected`.
The module doc (lines 15-17) describes dry mode as 'the run is a logged dry run', i.e. no results are implied.
detail.suggestion: Return early from run_scenario when `deps.dry` is true (or when execute reported a dry run) so no bas_results rows are written and no SUBJECT_DETECTION envelope is published; alternatively tag the payload/row with `dry_run=true` and have the detection-agent filter on it.

..summary: cancel_run's `rows_affected() == 0` early return is textually identical to the fall-through tail, so the guard changes nothing

evidence: crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:459-472 returns `load_run(...).map(...ACCEPTED...).ok_or_else(404)` when the UPDATE matched no row.
crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:473-484 repeats the exact same expression unconditionally, so the early return is dead weight and a reader must diff two 14-line blocks to see they agree.
detail.suggestion: Drop the `if updated.rows_affected() == 0 { ... }` block and rely on the single trailing load_run/404 path (the UPDATE result is only needed if you intend different status codes for 'already terminal' vs 'just cancelled').

..summary: An unrecognised VULN_MIN_SEVERITY ranks 0, which makes the severity filter always true instead of failing

evidence: crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:86-94: `severity_rank` returns 0 for any unknown string.

crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:221-228: `min_rank = severity_rank(&cfg.min_severity)` and `qualifies = severity_rank(&severity) >= min_rank || rec.has_kev || matched.is_some()`; with a typo such as `VULN_MIN_SEVERITY=hgih` every CVE (rank >= 0) qualifies and cases are opened for the whole NVD window.
The clap arg at :64-66 is a free-form String, so nothing rejects the typo earlier.
detail.suggestion: Parse `min_severity` once at startup into a validated enum (clap `value_parser` or a `match` returning an error) and abort boot on an unknown value, so the comparison can never degrade to `>= 0`.

..summary: forbidden_args classes are raw strings matched with `_ => false`, so a typo silently disables the IP-class check

evidence: crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:521-537 dispatches on class name literals ("RFC1918", "loopback", "multicast", "link_local", "unspecified", "cgNAT"/"shared") and returns `false` for anything else, so the check passes by default.
policies/tools.yml:129-130 supplies those names as free-form YAML (`ip: [RFC1918, loopback, multicast]`); `PolicyEngine::load` (lib.rs:268-301) never validates them.
The same file already types the sibling policy fields as serde enums (`Impact`, `Autonomy` at lib.rs:67-82), so the stricter pattern is right there.
detail.suggestion: Add `#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "...")] enum IpClass { Rfc1918, Loopback, Multicast, LinkLocal, Unspecified, Cgnat }`, type `forbidden_args: HashMap<String, Vec<IpClass>>`, and match on the enum exhaustively — an unknown class in tools.yml then fails `PolicyEngine::load` instead of quietly allowing the call.

..summary: Severity is a bare string in six modules with two fail-open rank parsers, so a config typo escalates every CVE

evidence: Two spellings of the same band: crates/cvss/src/lib.rs:44,53 yields `severity: &'static str` ("None"/"Low"/"Medium"/"High"/"Critical") while crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:825 keeps NVD's `Option<String>` ("HIGH").

crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:53 types the threshold as `String` and :86-94 maps it with `_ => 0`, so `VULN_MIN_SEVERITY=hgih` makes `severity_rank(&severity) >= min_rank` (:228) true for every CVE with a metric.
The same rank is written into `NewCase.severity: u8` (:258); an unrecognised band sends TheHive severity 0, outside its 1-4 range.

crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:60,66-68,256-261 adds a third mapping (`severity_gte_high`, the `open_case` match with `_ => 2`) and crates/api-server/src/vulns.rs:36-38 accepts `cvss_v4_severity`/`cvss_v3_severity` as free strings that are just uppercased.
detail.suggestion: Define one `Severity` enum (None/Low/Medium/High/Critical) with serde spellings and a `rank()`/`Ord` impl, parse the CLI/env threshold into it with clap `ValueEnum`, and replace `severity_rank`, `severity_gte_high` and the `open_case` match with the enum so invalid input fails at startup instead of becoming rank 0.

..summary: LLM verdict/severity are String fields matched against literals, and an unexpected value silently drops the alert

evidence: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:56-63 deserializes `Verdict { verdict: String, severity: String }` straight from model output, although the prompt at :71-76 defines the closed set `tp|fp|suspicious` and `low|medium|high|critical`.

crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:415-445 matches `verdict.verdict.as_str()`: `fp` writes the verdict doc, `tp`/`suspicious` open a case, and any other value hits `other => warn!("unrecognized verdict; logging only")` — the alert is dropped with no case.
The decision-model path (:175-192) copies `Choice.choice: String` (llm-client/src/systemone.rs:165-167) verbatim without checking it is one of `VERDICT_LABELS`.
detail.suggestion: Deserialize into `enum Verdict { Tp, Fp, Suspicious }` and `enum Severity` with `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]`; a hallucinated label then fails `serde_json::from_str` at :125 with the raw model output in the error instead of falling through a match arm.

..summary: CvssMetric fields are non-Option but parse_cve fills them with ""/0.0, and 0.0 is itself a valid CVSS score

evidence: crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:813-826 declares `version: String, source: String, kind: String, vector: String, base_score: f64` with no `Option`, promising fields the NVD payload may omit.
crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:1056-1063 fills them with `unwrap_or("")` / `unwrap_or(0.0)`, so 'absent' and 'empty'/'0.0' are indistinguishable at the type level.
crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:100 filters `m.base_score > 0.0`, which drops a genuine CVSS 0.0 (severity None) record and cannot distinguish it from a parse default.
detail.suggestion: Type the genuinely optional parts as `Option<String>`/`Option<f64>` (or have `parse_cve` skip a metric when `cvssData` is missing) and let callers decide the policy for an absent score instead of encoding absence as 0.0.

..summary: a2a/acp write protocol states as SQL literals and re-parse with lossy fallbacks instead of using the enums

evidence: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs writes `'working'` (:418), `'failed'` (:442), `'canceled'` (:486-487) and `'completed'` (:337, :617) while `TaskState::as_str()` (a2a/src/task.rs:44-53) is the canonical mapping and is only used for display (:441 in acp.rs, run_event).

crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:316 reads back with `TaskState::parse(&row.state).unwrap_or(TaskState::Submitted)`, so an unrecognised stored value becomes a live 'submitted' task that a client can re-drive.

crates/acp/src/lib.rs:172-182 maps every unknown status to `InProgress` (a completed run could be resurrected), and crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:85,452 keeps the same literals in the DDL and the cancel UPDATE.
detail.suggestion: Bind `TaskState::as_str()`/`RunStatus::as_str()` in the SQL statements, propagate parse failure instead of defaulting (`?` on the `Option` or `BackendError::Internal`), and add a CHECK constraint listing the enum's values so the TEXT column cannot drift from the enum.
